e: Parliamentary immunity for Prime Minister Magyar and two ministers from the Orbán era is suspended by the National Assembly.
The inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship is held in Budapest.
Ten Russian diplomats are expelled by Hungary for "unacceptable activities".
The rights and obligations of former kekva foundations are transferred to the state, except for those involved in higher education.
Dávid Vitézy declares Hungary has passed all conditions for unlocking its EU Recovery Funds by the deadline.
Anna Unger is elected president of NVVH.
A Saab JAS 39 Gripen fighter jet of the Hungarian Air Force crashes near Szolnok. The pilot ejects safely.
János Lázár resigns his parliamentary mandate.
András Baka is inaugurated as President.
The Constitutional Court rejects the complaints of Fidesz-KDNP over the removal of Sulyok
A bus carrying pilgrims returning from Bosnia-Herzegovina to Poland overturns and veers off the M3 into a ditch near Mezőkeresztes, killing 12 people and injuring 47 others.
Tisza nominates András Baka, former president of the Supreme Court of Hungary, to be President of the Republic.

The output of the Paks Nuclear Power Plant is reduced due to the extreme low water levels on the Danube. The government introduces emergency restrictions to cope with the resulting electricity shortage.
Parliament passes the law establishing the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH), which comes into effect next day.
MTVA officially closes down after a vote.
Chief Prosecutor Gábor Bálint Nagy resigns.
Minister of Transport and Investment Dávid Vitézy unveils a 3.550 trillion forint railway development program named after Gábor Baross.
Prosecutors seize Fidesz servers in relation to the Óbuda scandal.
Speaker of the National Assembly Ágnes Forsthoffer becomes acting President.
Chess grandmaster Judit Polgár declines Magyar's offer for the presidency.
President Sulyok signs the 17th constitutional amendment, ending his term as head of state.
Péter Szijjártó resigns his parliamentary mandate to work for BYD.
Orsolya Ferencz, supported by Tibor Navracsics, declares the need for a new political community outside Fidesz.
Parliament passes the 17th Amendment to the Fundamental Law, allowing for the removal of President Sulyok and Constitutional Court President Péter Polt.
Gergely Gulyás resigns as the leader of Fidesz's parliamentary group.
Thousands of people protest in Budapest against attempts by Prime Minister Magyar to oust president Sulyok.
M1 suspends news broadcasts amid government efforts to overhaul the public broadcasting sector on neutrality grounds.
Parliament abolishes the Sovereignty Protection Office, effective July 15.
Magyar announces the 17th Amendment to the Fundamental Law, dubbed "Operation Cleansing Fire", aimed to remove Sulyok from power.
The European Council approves Hungary's RRF plan.
The government lifts a ban on 12 Ukrainian newspapers that was imposed during Orbán's premiership in 2025.

Seven judges of the Constitutional Court refuse to participate in the upcoming hearting of Sulyok's petition against his removal. In lieu of quorum, Péter Polt removes the case from the court's agenda.

Parliament passes the 16th Amendment to the Fundamental Law, establishing an eight-year term limit for the Prime Minister. It also establishes the legal basis for abolishing kekva foundations and the Sovereignty Protection Office.
Viktor Orbán is reelected as leader of Fidesz.
A minibus collides with a truck that had been stalled on a highway near Győr due to an earlier collision that left one person dead, killing an additional seven people.
Parliament passes a package of anti-corruption measures required to unlock RRF funds.
Protest in front of Sándor Palace, against the removal of Sulyok and other state officials.
